arxiv-2006-14973.title: Fluid Drag Reduction by Magnetic Confinement
arxiv-2006-14973.creator: Arvind Arun Dev, Peter Dunne, Thomas M. Hermans, Bernard Doudin
arxiv-2006-14973.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Arvind Arun Dev, Peter Dunne, Thomas M. Hermans, Bernard Doudin. The frictional forces of a viscous liquid flow are a major energy loss issue and severely limit microfluidics practical use. Reducing this drag by more than a few tens of percent remain elusive. Here, we show how cylindrical liquid–in–liquid flow leads to drag reduction of 60–99% for sub-mm and mm-sized channels, regardless of whether the viscosity of the transported liquid is larger or smaller than that of the confining one.

arxiv-2201-01567.title: Selective nuclear-spin interaction based on a dissipatively stabilized nitrogen-vacancy center
arxiv-2201-01567.creator: Jiawen Jiang and Q. Chen
arxiv-2201-01567.description: Abstract Current typical methods to realize nuclear-nuclear quantum gates require a sequence of electron-nuclear quantum gates by using dynamical decoupling techniques, which are implemented at low temperature because of short decoherence and relaxation time of the NV spin at room temperature.

arxiv-2211-11006.title: Regularity of solutions to the Muskat equation
arxiv-2211-11006.creator: Jia Shi
arxiv-2211-11006.description: Abstract In this paper, we show that if a solution to the Muskat problem in the case of different densities and the same viscosity is sufficiently smooth, then it must be analytic except at the points where a turnover of the fluids happens.

arxiv-2312-17132.title: Bootstrapping Smooth Conformal Defects in Chern-Simons-Matter Theories
arxiv-2312-17132.creator: Barak Gabai, Amit Sever, and De-liang Zhong
arxiv-2312-17132.description: Abstract The expectation value of a smooth conformal line defect in a CFT is a conformal invariant functional of its path in space-time. For example, in large N N holographic theories, these fundamental observables are dual to the open-string partition function in AdS.

arxiv-2405-15263.title: Point-set games and functions with the hereditary small oscillation property
arxiv-2405-15263.creator: Marek Balcerzak, Tomasz Natkaniec, Piotr Szuca
arxiv-2405-15263.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Marek Balcerzak, Tomasz Natkaniec, Piotr Szuca. Given a metric space X X , we consider certain families of functions f : X → ℝ f\colon X\to\mathbb{R} having the hereditary oscillation property HSOP and the hereditary continuous restriction property HCRP on large sets. When X X is Polish, among them there are families of Baire measurable functions, μ ¯ \overline{\mu} -measurable functions (for a finite nonatomic Borel measure μ \mu on X X ) and Marczewski measurable functions.

arxiv-2507-06134.title: OpenAgentSafety : A Comprehensive Framework for Evaluating Real-World AI Agent Safety
arxiv-2507-06134.creator: Sanidhya Vijayvargiya, Aditya Bharat Soni, Xuhui Zhou, Zora Zhiruo Wang, Nouha Dziri, Graham Neubig, Maarten Sap
arxiv-2507-06134.description: Abstract Recent advances in AI agents capable of solving complex, everyday tasks—from scheduling to customer service—have enabled deployment in real-world settings, but their possibilities for unsafe behavior demands rigorous evaluation. While prior benchmarks have attempted to assess agent safety, most fall short by relying on simulated environments, narrow task domains, or unrealistic tool abstractions.

pmc-10535577.title: Organic Compounds Responsible for the Fouling of Ultrafiltration Membrane Treating Algae-Laden Water
pmc-10535577.creator: Edwin Castilla-Rodriguez, Hongde Zhou, Weichen Lin
pmc-10535577.description: Fouling comparisons of the organic fractions in surface and algae-laden waters make it possible to determine the main compounds responsible for the fouling of ultrafiltration (UF) membranes. This study examined the fouling of UF membranes and its relationship to the characteristics of the organic fractions found in drinking-water supply.

pmc-10738932.title: DEPRESSION AND ROLE OVERLOAD IN FAMILY CAREGIVERS OF PEOPLE LIVING WITH AND WITHOUT DEMENTIA
pmc-10738932.creator: Claire McDonald, Adrian Bravo
pmc-10738932.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The present study examined the associations between caregiver assistance, role overload as a stressor, and depression symptoms among caregivers of adults age 65 and older living with and without probable dementia. Specifically, we hypothesized that more time spent caregiving would be associated with higher depressive symptoms via greater role overload and this indirect association would be stronger for those caregiving for an older adult with probable dementia versus no probable dementia.

pmc-12430290.title: Biocontrol Potential of Rhizobacteria Against Passalora fulva and Tuta absoluta: A Sustainable Approach for Tomato Protection
pmc-12430290.creator: Said Bahoch, Abdessamad Elaasri, Salahddine Chafiki, Fouad Elame, Ahmed Wifaya, El hassan Mayad, Rachid Bouharroud, Redouan Qessaoui, Jill M Farrant, Shandry M Tebele
pmc-12430290.description: Plant growth-promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) offer a sustainable strategy for enhancing crop productivity and suppressing phytopathogens. In this study, seven bacterial isolates obtained from the rhizosphere of healthy tomato plants were evaluated for their antagonistic activity against the fungal pathogen Passalora fulva, the leaf miner Tuta absoluta, and their effects on tomato growth.

pmc-12622725.title: Epidemiological trends, attributable risks, decomposition analysis, and forecasts of Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias burden in China, 1990 to 2036: A population-based observational study
pmc-12622725.creator: Haigang Chang
pmc-12622725.description: This study analyzes the burden of Alzheimer disease and other dementias (ADOD) in China using Global Burden of Disease 2021 data. The data on ADOD in China from 1990 to 2021 was collected from the Global Burden of Disease 2021. The incidence rate, mortality and the number of disability adjusted life years (DALYs), and age-standardized rates of ADOD were analyzed.

pmc-12649520.title: Multicentric Surveillance of Antimicrobial Resistance to Generate Data-Driven Regional Antibiograms: A Laboratory-Based Cross-Sectional Study in Pakistan
pmc-12649520.creator: Nadia Noreen, Adeel Aslam, Mateen Abbas, Asma Ghulam Mustafa, Shazia Jamshed, Márió Gajdács, Ayesha Iqbal, Wajid Syed, Adel Bashatah, Naji Alqahtani, Majdi N Al-Hasan
pmc-12649520.description: Background: The escalating burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a critical threat to public health in Pakistan, with rates of high antibiotic consumption and limited standardized surveillance on AMR rates. Our study aimed to carry out a multicentric surveillance of AMR to generate regional antibiograms for Northern Punjab, Pakistan, to guide empirical antimicrobial therapy and stewardship efforts.

pmc-12656652.title: SenseBike: A New Low-Cost Mobile-Networked Sensor System for Cyclists to Monitor Air Quality and Automatically Measure Passing Distances in Urban Traffic
pmc-12656652.creator: Andre Tenbeitel, Simone Arnold, Jens Rettkowski
pmc-12656652.description: This study presents the development and validation of a low-cost, open-source sensor system for cyclists that automatically detects vehicle overtaking events while simultaneously monitoring air quality. The system integrates multiple ultrasonic sensors for autonomous overtaking detection and distance measurement with environmental sensors that record particulate matter, temperature, humidity, and GPS position.

pmc-12732183.title: A Machine Learning Model to Reframe the Concept of Shelf-Life in Bakery Products: PDO Sourdough as a Technological Preservation Model
pmc-12732183.creator: Andrea Marianelli, Cecilia Akotowaa Offei, Monica Macaluso, Nicola Mercanti, Bruno Casu, Angela Zinnai, Weiqing Min
pmc-12732183.description: Traditional shelf-life (SL) determination in bakery products relies primarily on subjective sensory evaluation, limiting both predictive capability and technological transfer. This study aimed to develop an objective, data-driven framework by integrating statistical and Machine Learning (ML) methods to identify and quantify the core determinants of bread SL.

pmc-13462601.title: Genetic associations between post-traumatic stress disorder and REM-sleep behavior disorder
pmc-13462601.creator: Morvarid Ghamgosar Shahkhali, Lang Liu, Mohammad H. Ghamgosar Shahkhali, Eric Yu, Farnaz Asayesh, Jamil Ahmad, Meron Teferra, Isabelle Arnulf, Pauline Dodet, Yo-El Ju, Michele T. M. Hu, Jacques Y. Montplaisir, Jean-François Gagnon, Alex Desautels, Abubaker Ibrahim, Ambra Stefani, Birgit Högl, Merve
pmc-13462601.description: Isolated/idiopathic rapid-eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) is, in most cases, an early form of α -synuclein-related neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson’s disease and dementia with Lewy bodies. Clinical reports suggest that iRBD is more common in individuals with Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) compared to those without PTSD.

pmc-13556656.title: 545. Targeting negative and cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia: discussion of novel preclinical and clinical findings with evenamide
pmc-13556656.creator: R Anand, A Turolla, G Chinellato, F Sansi, R Hartman
pmc-13556656.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe recognition of hippocampal pyramidal neuron hyperexcitability as core pathological feature of schizophrenia has led to the idea that the hippocampus might be a promising target for therapeutic intervention (Lodge and Grace, 2011). However, the mechanism of action (MoA) of currently available antipsychotics (AP) is mainly based on dopamine/serotonin modulation occurring downstream from the hippocampus; this may explain why their efficacy is limited only to positive symptoms, while they have failed to provide meaningful improvements of negative symptoms and cognitive deficits.

pmc-13579570.title: Changes in fatty acid and mineral profiles of the turkey egg yolk-yolk sac complex during embryonic development
pmc-13579570.creator: Leila Fathi, Maghsoud Besharati, Zabihollah Nemati, Reza Asadpour, Lucrezia Forte, Aristide Maggiolino, Gerardo Centoducati, Giusy Rusco
pmc-13579570.description: The yolk–yolk sac complex is the main nutrient source for the avian embryo and undergoes marked compositional changes during incubation. However, information on mineral and fatty acid dynamics in turkey eggs remains limited. This study evaluated changes in mineral concentrations, absolute mineral contents, and fatty acid composition of the turkey egg yolk–yolk sac complex during embryonic development.

pmc-13665602.title: Improved impact from the use of beneficial natural enemy species in Australian canola systems: challenges and required tools
pmc-13665602.creator: Sarina Macfadyen, Basman Al‐Jalely, Mukti Chalise, Maryam Ehsangar, Zorica Duric, Joanne Holloway, Andrew Hulthen, Precious Mavende, Paul Melloy, Svetlana Micic, Hazel Parry, Shovon Chandra Sarkar, Jessa Thurman, Maarten Van Helden, Xiaobei Wang, Wei Xu
pmc-13665602.description: The concept of Integrated Pest Management (IPM) has developed into a practical framework for sustainable pest management and is widely adopted in modern farming systems. Beneficial arthropods (natural enemies, such as predators and parasitoids) have shown potential for use in pest management, leading to observable production benefits.
